r0.why: Rock-forming, made of silicate groups (1); largest and most important class, about 90 percent of the crust (2).

r1.why: Subunit formula (11), tetrahedral silicon with four oxides (18), anion simplification (12), balancing cations (13-14), Si-O-M bonds (15).

r2.why: Anions colorless, white as powder (16); color from the metal component, commonly iron (17).

r3.why: Variety and combinations from billions of years of crust processes (6), and the six processes are listed in 7.

r4.why: Organisms contribute (8), diatoms build frustules from seawater silica (9), frustules in ocean sediment and diatomaceous earth (10).

r5.why: Silica as quartz (5), tectosilicates under Dana (3), oxides under Nickel-Strunz (4), aluminum substitution (20-21).
